paper_metadata.title: Mixed-Signal Quantum Circuit Design for Option Pricing Using Design Compiler

summary: This paper presents a gate-based quantum circuit optimization study for option pricing, reporting a reduction in gate count from 4095 to 392 and depth from 2048 to 6 for a 12-qubit QAE-based data-preprocessing circuit. It also describes a Monte Carlo-style price simulation circuit using Hadamard-generated randomness and optional QAE, but the paper does not demonstrate practical quantum advantage or a hardware run, and the nonlinear exponential/payoff components are explicitly not yet implemented.

experiments.description: Gate-based quantum circuit optimization for option-pricing data pre-processing using Synopsys Design Compiler, benchmarked against the JP Morgan QAE option-pricing circuit.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Amplitude Estimation (QAE) option-pricing circuit optimization

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 12-qubit input case; RTL-encoded lognormal distribution values mapped to thread IDs 0 to 4095 and used as inputs to the synthesized circuit; rotation-gate based data preprocessing for weighted averaging in option pricing.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Compute weighted averages for option pricing via QAE-based averaging circuit.

problem_instance.description: 12-qubit option-pricing data pre-processing case study comparing the proposed design with JP Morgan's circuit.

dataset_specification.description: Lognormal probability distribution discretized into 32 output levels (0 to 31) with inputs ranging from 0 to 4095.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Classical preprocessing of the piecewise linear payoff region; RTL encoding of the lognormal distribution; Design Compiler synthesis of the circuit.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Comparison against JP Morgan's circuit on gate count, depth, and error rate.

noise_model.noise_type: analog inaccuracies / noise sensitivity in rotation gates

noise_model.mitigation_details: Digital calibration via lookup-table correction and arcsin-based angle adjustment; reported maximum calculation error reduced from 25.86% to 1.64%.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical preprocessing isolates the payoff region where payoff exceeds strike price; RTL encoding of lognormal distribution.

speedup_claims.caveats: Reported as gate-count reduction from 4095 to 392; this is an optimization result for preprocessing, not an end-to-end option-pricing speedup.
Reported as depth reduction from 2048 to 6; not a proven runtime speedup on hardware.

speedup_claims.conditions: digital calibration on rotation-gate usage range 0 to pi/2 radians
speedup_claims.caveats: Maximum calculation error reduced from 25.86% to 1.64%; the paper attributes this to LUT-based digital calibration.
The paper states this as an expected complexity improvement; no formal proof or scaling experiment is provided.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(n^2) data preprocessing and O(n) depth (claimed for optimized preprocessing)

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No hardware execution or end-to-end benchmark against a classical option-pricing solver is reported; only circuit-level reductions are given.
limiting_factors: Nonlinear payoff/exponential components are not implemented
Reported gains are circuit-optimization metrics, not application-level advantage

notes: No specific QPU or simulator is named; hardware.type is left not_specified and framework is inferred from the paper's use of Qiskit for histogram/statevector analysis.
The paper reports a 12-qubit case study and gate/depth reductions; the experiment is gate-based because it uses QAE and quantum circuits, not annealing.
The claimed complexity improvement is for data preprocessing, not a proven end-to-end asymptotic speedup over a classical option-pricing algorithm.

The paper reports gate count reduction from 4095 to 392 and depth from 2048 to 6 for a 12-qubit case study, but does not demonstrate practical quantum advantage over a classical option-pricing method.

experiments.description: Mixed-signal gate-based Monte Carlo price simulation circuit for option pricing, with direct measurement and QAE-based measurement discussed as evaluation modes.

algorithm.variant: Monte Carlo price simulation with QAE measurement option

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Quantum random number generation via Hadamard gates and measurement; single-qubit price accumulator used instead of a multi-bit digital accumulator; QAE can be used for final averaging.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Simulate multi-day asset price fluctuations and compute the expected average stock price / option-pricing average.

problem_instance.description: Monte Carlo-based option pricing / random-walk price simulation.

dataset_specification.description: Random walk generator for 1-day and 2-day price distributions; zero probability for unchanged asset prices (+0%) used for consistency checks.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Random fluctuations generated from a predefined probability distribution function; cumulative price changes accumulated over time; final prices averaged across runs.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Comparison of quantum Monte Carlo histograms/statevector outputs against classical Monte Carlo results for 1-day and 2-day price distributions.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical Monte Carlo baseline and probability distribution specification; the paper also notes that nonlinear exponential/payoff components are not yet implemented.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Averaging of simulated payoffs / stock prices; histogram comparison with classical Monte Carlo.

speedup_claims.conditions: when QAE is used for final averaging
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper claims QAE can reduce measurements and enable quantum advantages, but provides no formal end-to-end speedup proof or measured oracle-query count.
The reported Monte Carlo results are consistency checks against classical Monte Carlo; no quantitative speedup is demonstrated.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Massively parallel simulation with QAE reducing measurements; no explicit asymptotic bound given for the full Monte Carlo circuit.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: The paper compares simulated quantum Monte Carlo outputs with classical Monte Carlo histograms and states consistency, but provides no measured speedup or resource advantage.
limiting_factors: No hardware execution or timing data
Nonlinear exponential/payoff components are not implemented
QAE is discussed as an option, but not benchmarked as an advantage
Classical Monte Carlo remains a valid baseline with matching outputs

notes: The paper discusses a gate-based quantum Monte Carlo circuit with Hadamard gates, measurements, and optional QAE; no annealer is involved.
No explicit qubit count, depth, or shot count is reported for this Monte Carlo experiment, so these fields are left null/inferred only at the algorithm level.
The paper states that QAE can be used to reduce measurements, but does not provide a formal end-to-end speedup proof.
The paper states the quantum Monte Carlo simulation is consistent with classical Monte Carlo, but does not show superiority; the comparison is qualitative and simulation-based.
